outroLine: Connect the ways orders already reach you.

beats.shot: Land on /settings, Organization tab. Cursor rests on the 'How do you use ProcuLink?' direction cards (send to suppliers / receive from customers).
beats.vo: Settings starts with a question that shapes the whole product. Do you send purchase orders to your suppliers, or receive them from your customers? ProcuLink works in both directions — this sets how the parties are labelled across the app.

beats.shot: Click Email intake: the IMAP mailbox form; cursor types a host; the 'unseen messages with CSV, XLSX, or PDF attachments are imported' note is on screen.
beats.vo: If orders arrive by email today, point ProcuLink at the mailbox. Unseen messages with order attachments are picked up automatically, every few minutes. No forwarding, no copy-paste.

beats.shot: Click SFTP pull: host/port/credentials/folder form, default supplier select, and the 'secrets are encrypted and never shown again' footer.
beats.vo: The same goes for file drops. Poll an S F T P folder for order files, attribute them to a supplier — and secrets are encrypted, never shown again.

beats.shot: Click S3 / R2 pull: the bucket polling form.
beats.vo: Or pull from an S 3 compatible bucket, if that's where your systems already drop order files.

beats.shot: Click API keys: the workspace ingress endpoint; cursor clicks Create key, types a label, creates it — the one-time key banner appears.
beats.vo: For real integrations there's the REST A P I. Your workspace has its own ingress endpoint, and keys authenticate it. A key is shown exactly once, at creation — copy it then, because it cannot be retrieved again.

beats.shot: Click Connectors: REST API & webhooks card, the honest 'Coming soon' on native Zapier/Make apps, and the Add webhook affordance.
beats.vo: And webhooks push events out the moment they happen — to your own backend, or into a Zapier or Make scenario today. The native one-click apps are marked coming soon, because what's offered on this screen is only ever what already works.
